prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: full level-map concept for Snabbit, a real 2D upward-scrolling game on a staggered 16-column hex grid.
Primary request: Design one beautiful, gentle introductory lever level called "First Light". The player starts at bottom near column 9, moves upward with diagonal left/right steering. Make an authored, pleasing asymmetric composition of irregular silver asteroid clusters floating in deep navy space, with abundant breathing room. The central idea is one big broken crescent of chunky asteroids: a welcoming open lower bay, a chunky orange lever on its lower-right shoulder, then a soft leftward bend through a short local gate in the crescent into a sheltered upper cove and finish. One lever opens that single gate. Place exactly three clearly separated golden stars along the enjoyable sweeping route, a handful of cyan gems as small accents, not a continuous lane. The first star greets the player before the lever, the second draws them through the gate, the third sits in the upper cove. The finish is a short thin glowing line at the top of the cove. Give enough room around each action for easy turns.
Input images: Image 1 is a contact sheet of genuine opening levels from packs 10/20/30: use their original spare game-map language, irregular masses, isolated mechanical events and open dark space. Image 2 is the genuine game sprite sheet: use these exact silver faceted metal stones, occasional dark rocks and brown dirt, cyan gems, golden stars and chunky grey lever with orange knob. The lever occupies only one grid cell; draw it a little larger than a rock for readability.
Style/medium: crisp flat 2D game screenshot/map using the actual source-sprite look, no perspective, no painterly landscape, no invented terrain or decoration. Individual repeated sprites read as chunky separate stones. All rock centers follow a staggered offset-hex layout, exactly 16 columns wide and roughly 48 rows tall. No visible grid needed.
Composition/framing: one complete tall portrait map, bottom is entrance, top is finish; generous navy border. No UI, labels, headings, arrows, paths, legends or text. The gate is a tiny group of 3–4 orange-outlined silver rocks occupying only the local opening between two irregular masses. Keep it visually unmistakable, without full-width walls. Asteroid clusters should have a natural hand-placed silhouette, little bites and protrusions, unequal sizes and varied spacing. Use silver mass on the lower left balanced by a smaller right shoulder and upper crescent.
Lighting/mood: quiet, playful, inviting, luminous but restrained.
Avoid: straight gem runway, long rails, repeated full-width wall rows, regular zigzag, endless maze, symmetry, too many levers, sci-fi machinery, new artwork, long continuous neon path, tiny unreadable objects, decorative nebula overpowering the gameplay.
Refinement from more complete genuine opening-level references (Images 3–5): make the image more compact, approximately 16 columns by 48 rows, so its full-map height is about 1.7 times its width, not a very long scrolling strip. Keep the wonderful irregular crescent. Put the lever in a clear little opening beside the right shoulder rather than buried inside stone; the snabbit must be able to collect it from below and leave above. The second star should be immediately above the short three-stone gate, not below it. Make the final goal a few small gold finish sparkles across only two or three cells, matching original goal art, not a cyan finish bar. Exactly three golden stars total.
